title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
summary: Given a linked list and an integer k, swap the values of the kth node from the start and the kth node from the end, both 1-indexed, and return the modified list.
statement: Given a linked list and an integer k, swap the values of the kth node from the start and the kth node from the end, both 1-indexed, and return the modified list.
constraints: The list is nonempty and k is between one and its length.
Swap the values of the kth node from the start and kth node from the end, preserving the original nodes and links.
reference_solution:
def swap_kth_node_values(head, k):
 first=head
 for _ in range(k-1):first=first.next
 fast=first;second=head
 while fast.next:fast=fast.next;second=second.next
 first.val,second.val=second.val,first.val
 return head

hints: Once the kth node is found, the kth-from-end node can be located by preserving that lead gap.
Advance first k-1 steps; move a fast pointer from first and a second pointer from head until fast reaches the tail.
Swap only first.val and second.val, then return the unchanged head.
The two moving pointers keep a k-1 edge gap, so when fast is last, second is kth from the end.

tests.explanation: The second nodes from the front and back hold two and four, producing [1,4,3,2,5].
The first and last values swap, producing [9,7].
